title: knapsack, subset-sum, and resource-allocation DP
concepts: Knapsack DP chooses items subject to a capacity or resource budget; the state records which items remain eligible and how much capacity is available.
In 0/1 knapsack each item may be selected once, so a one-dimensional capacity loop runs downward to avoid reusing the current item.
In unbounded knapsack an item may be reused, so a one-dimensional capacity loop commonly runs upward; loop order encodes the reuse rule.
Subset sum asks whether selected values reach a target and is a special boolean knapsack recurrence; reachable sums can be represented with a boolean array or bitset.
Partition equal subset sum first checks that the total is even, then asks whether a subset reaches half the total; this reduction should be proved before applying the DP.
Target-sum counting can map plus/minus assignments to a subset-sum count when parity and range conditions are satisfied.
The O(nW) dynamic program is pseudo-polynomial because it depends on numeric capacity W rather than the number of bits needed to encode W.
When reconstructing selected items, preserve predecessor choices or use a carefully justified recomputation; equal-value choices may produce multiple optimal subsets.

practiceProblems.name: Partition Equal Subset Sum
patterns: reduce to subset sum at half total
practiceProblems.statement: Return whether the positive integers in nums can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sums; every array element is used exactly once.

practiceProblems.name: Target Sum
practiceProblems.statement: Place either '+' or '-' before every nums element and return the number of resulting expressions whose value equals target. Each index receives exactly one sign, including zero-valued entries.

practiceProblems.name: Coin Change II
practiceProblems.statement: Given distinct positive coin denominations and an amount, return the number of combinations that make the amount when an unlimited number of each coin is available. Different orders of the same coin multiset count as one combination. The answer fits a signed 32-bit integer.

practiceProblems.name: Last Stone Weight II
patterns: minimize difference from reachable half sums
practiceProblems.statement: Repeatedly smash any two stones of weights x<=y: equal weights disappear; otherwise x disappears and y becomes y-x. Return the smallest possible final stone weight, or zero if none remains.

practiceProblems.name: Ones and Zeroes
practiceProblems.statement: Given binary strings strs and budgets m zeroes and n ones, return the largest subset size whose total zero count is at most m and total one count is at most n.

practiceProblems.name: Combination Sum IV
patterns: outer target loop changes ordering semantics
practiceProblems.statement: Given distinct positive integers nums and target, return the number of ordered sequences (reusing values any number of times) whose sum is target. Different orders count as different combinations; the answer fits a signed 32-bit integer.
